sentences.text: Per: Justice Ratnesh Chandra Singh Bisen This appeal is filed by the State being aggrieved of judgment dated 13.06.2022 passed by learned Sessions Judge, District Narmadapuram (M.P.) in S.T. No.31/2019, whereby learned trial Court has acquitted the accused persons/respondents from the charges under Sections 498A and 304-B of IPC, giving the benefit of doubt.

2. Learned Government Advocate for the State submits that the impugned judgment dated 13.06.2022 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, District Narmadapuram in Sessions Trial No.31/2019 acquitting the respondents/accused from offences under Sections 498A and 304-B NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:25709 2 CRA-9013-2022 of IPC is illegal, perverse,
and contrary to law, as the learned Trial Court failed to properly appreciate the material evidence on record.

It is further submitted that the prosecution case clearly establishes that the deceased Anuradha @ Aarti Solanki, who was married to Pawan Solanki on 24.02.2014, sustained burn injuries on 29.09.2018 at her matrimonial home and was admitted to Narmada Apna Hospital,
The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Sanjay @ Sonu Solanki on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128294985/
1 Narmadapuram, where she died during treatment on 01.10.2018, and thereafter Marg No. 62/2018 was registered and investigation was carried out, during which the spot was inspected in the presence of the FSL officer and incriminating articles such as half-burnt clothes, kerosene residue,
broken mangalsutra pieces and matchsticks were seized.

sentences.text: Statements of the deceased's mother Prembai, father Vrindavan Bathri and brothers Mukesh and Naresh Bathri were recorded, who consistently deposed that the deceased was subjected to continuous cruelty and harassment by the respondents in connection with dowry demands and that on the date of incident, following a dispute instigated by the aunt Tulsabai and other in-laws.
The deceased being mentally and physically tortured, committed suicide by pouring kerosene upon herself.
Despite such cogent, reliable and unshaken evidence proving that the death occurred under unnatural circumstances within seven years of marriage and soon after dowry-related harassment.
In these circumstances, the impugned judgment of acquittal is liable to be set aside and the respondents deserve to be convicted.

3. Learned counsel for respondents/accused opposed the prayer NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:25709 3 CRA-9013-2022 and submitted that the judgment dated 13.06.2022 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Narmadapuram, acquitting the respondents is legal and well-reasoned, as the prosecution failed to prove the charges under Sections 498A and 304-B IPC beyond reasonable doubt.

The allegations of dowry demand and cruelty are vague and based solely on interested witnesses with material contradictions and there is no reliable evidence to establish harassment soon before death or any proximate link between the alleged cruelty and the death of the deceased.
In these circumstances, the acquittal being based on proper appreciation of evidence calls for no interference and the appeal deserves to be dismissed.

4. Heard the counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5 .

Vrindavan Bathri (PW-6) , who is father of deceased Aarti Bathri, deposed that his daughter Aarti Bathri was married to Pawan Solanki on 24.02.2014 in Itarsi with great pomp and show as per his capacity.
After the wedding, Aarti Bathri was sent away to her in-law's house.
For a couple of months after the wedding, his daughter lived well at her in-laws' house.

Her brother-in-law Sonu,
mother-in-law Mayabai, and Pawan mentally harassed her for dowry.
Before the wedding, he was unaware that his son-in-law Pawan had a drinking habit.
Pawan used to beat his daughter.
Whenever Aarti's aunt-in-law Tulsabai would come to Aarti's in-laws' house in Hoshangabad from Mandi Bamora, she used to instigate her in-laws against her.
His daughter Aarti would tell him that she does not want to live in Hoshangabad anymore.

She want to live at NEUTRAL CITATION NO.

her maternal
home in Itarsi
. He persuaded to Aarti that a girl has to live in her in-laws' house, then after convincing her, he sent her from Itarsi to her in-laws' house at Hoshangabad.
He stated that his daughter continued to endure the pain and torture of her in-laws.
On 29.09.2018, Pawan called his younger son Naresh Kumar in Itarsi and told that his sister has been burned in the kitchen.
There was no kitchen where the fire broke out.
His son and his wife reached the girl at Narmada Hospital, Hoshangabad, before him.
Aarti told her mother Prembai that Pawan had said that if she gave a statement against him, her son would be homeless.
Kanha is his daughter's young child.
He arrived at Narmada Hospital, Hoshangabad, at 4-5 O'clock in the evening and saw that the daughter was being treated, covered and was not speaking.

His wife Prembai told him that Aarti had told her that Pawan had told her that if she gave The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Sanjay @ Sonu Solanki on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128294985/

sentences.text: His younger son Naresh Kumar and he stayed overnight at the Narmada Hospital in Hoshangabad.
His daughter Aarti died on the next day night on the 1st date during treatment.
The police conducted the paperwork on the 2n d date.

They also inspected the site where the girl was burned at her in-laws'
house.
The police recovered broken beads from a necklace, a burnt green cloth and a five-liter oil container from the place of occurrence.
The police had the room unlocked.
Upon entering, they found a matchstick and a matchbox.
A half-burnt sari and pieces of a guriya were also found.
They seized these articles and prepared seizure memos (Ex.P-8 and Ex.P-9).

Prem Bai Bathri (PW-3), who is mother of deceased Aarti Bathri, Mukesh Bathri (PW-4) and Naresh Kumar Bathri (PW-1), who are brother of deceased Aarti Bathri, deposed in their examination-in- chief the same version like Vrindavan Bathri (PW-6).
7. Chhotu Malviya (PW-2) deposed that he is acquainted with Aarti's father, Vrindavan Bathri (PW-6), whose house is situated opposite his own.
He also stated that he came to know that Aarti had been burned and was admitted in Narmada Hospital, Hoshangabad.
He went to hospital to see Aarti and met her, but she was unable to speak, then he returned.
She subsequently died within two to three days.
Thereafter, he visited her matrimonial home along with her family members, where he observed a sealed upstairs storeroom.
The police opened the room and seized a half-burnt saree, a burnt matchstick, a matchbox, a partially burnt mangalsutra and certain containers in his presence and prepared seizure memo (Ex.P-1).
He admitted in his cross- examination that deceased Aarti used to come to his house and tell him that her husband, mother-in-law and aunt-in-law harassed her for dowry.
He did not know how Aarti died.
He came to know that Aarti had doused herself in kerosene oil and set herself on fire.
8. Naresh Kumar Bathri (PW-1), brother of deceased Aarti, deposed that he received a phone call from Pawan Solanki informing him that his sister had sustained burn injuries.

Upon inquiring about the cause, he did not provide any explanation and asked him to come to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:25709 6 CRA-9013-2022 Hoshangabad.

He first went to New Pandey Hospital but did not find her there, then he learnt that she had been taken to Narmada Hospital,
Hoshangabad, where he saw her undergoing treatment.
He admitted in para 15 of his cross-examination that they did not lodge any report against the accused person that they had harassed her sister for dowry.
He also admitted that they did not lodge any report regarding the beating Aarti by her husband after drinking wine.
He also admitted in para 20 that when he visited to his sister's in-laws house, he lived well there.

9. Prem Bai Bathri (PW-3) stated in para 9 of her cross- examination that in her police statement (Ex.D/4) she stated that deceased's aunt-in-law used to say that she was an unlucky face, and that ever since she had set foot in her house, her brother had been paralyzed.
She stated that even during the delivery, her daughter's aunt-in-law quarreled with the girl and instructed her to take the delivery expenses from her parents.
If these details were not recorded in her police statement (Ex.D/4), she cannot explain why.

She also stated that she had stated in her police statement The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Sanjay @ Sonu Solanki on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128294985/
3 (Ex.D/4) that her daughter once made tea and placed it on the table for her brother-in-law Sonu.

sentences.text: As soon as she turned back, Sonu threw the glass of tea at her, causing burns.
Looking to the entire depositions of this witness, there are many contradictions and omissions present in the court statement and the statement Ex.D-1 which was recorded during the investigation.

10. Father of deceased Vrindavan Bathri (PW-6) admitted in para 8 of his cross-examination that he gave the items in he marriage of his NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:25709 7 CRA-9013-2022 daughter voluntarily.
He also admitted in para 13 that when he reached the Narmada Hospital, Hoshangabad, there was no conversation with deceased Aarti and he also admitted that Aarti was unable to speak at that time.
Aarti did not talk to anybody before him.
He also admitted in para 14 that when he reached the hospital after that post-mortem of her daughter was conducted and he also participated in the cremation of her daughter.
After cremation of her daughter, he did not lodge the report at the police station that the in-laws of her daughter killed her by set her on fire.
When her daughter came to Itarsi and told that she did not want to live in her in-laws' house at Hoshangabad.
At that time, he did not lodge any report.
He also admitted in para 22 of his cross-examination that they did not report against the accused person regarding the demand of dowry by accused persons before his daughter's death.
11. Shyam Rao Panse (PW-5) deposed that on 01.10.2018, he was posted as Head Constable at Police Station Kotwali, Hoshangabad.

On that date, Mukesh Chaure, an ambulance driver from Narmada Apna Hospital, Hoshangabad, came to the police station with a death memo issued by Dr. S.K.
Gupta, on the basis of which he registered original Marg No. 62/2018 under Section 174 of the Criminal Procedure Code, which is Ex.P-7.
He admitted in para 2 that it is mentioned in Ex.P-7 that the deceased had suffered burns while cooking and subsequently died during treatment.

12. Dr. Sharad Gupta (PW-8) deposed that he was posted as NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:25709 8 CRA-9013-2022 Doctor in Narmada Apna Hospital, Hoshangabad on 29.09.2018.
On said date, at around 2:10 P.M., Pawan Solanki brought his wife Anuradha @ Aarti for treatment of burn injuries.
Pawan Solanki informed him that the injuries were caused while she was cooking.
Upon examination, he found that deceased Anuradha had burnt about 99%.
Looking to the condition of patient after giving first aid treatment, he admitted in burn ward in the hospital.
He prepared the MLC report (Ex.P-12) and instructed his assistant Dr. Pradeep Rathore to send written information to the Kotwali Police Station, Hoshangabad, which is Ex.P-13.

During treatment,
Anuradha alias Aarti died on 01.10.2018 at 9:22 PM.
A written information of her death was sent to the Police Station, which is Ex.P-14.

He admitted in para 5 that it is mentioned in MLC report (Ex.P-12) deceased was burnt while cooking food in the kitchen, but he himself stated that the aforesaid was mentioned by telling deceased's husband Pawan.

13. Dr. R.K. Verma (PW-9) deposed that on 02.10.2018, he was posted as a Medical Officer at the District Hospital, Hoshangabad and he conducted the post-mortem of the deceased Aarti's body and he opined that the deceased died due to cardiac arrest as a complication of the burn injuries sustained and death occurred within 24 hours.
The deceased had received treatment at the hospital prior to death.
His report is Ex.P-16.
He admitted in his cross-examination that no smell of kerosene was detected on the body or clothing of the deceased at the time of post-mortem examination.

sentences.text: Mohan Sarwan (PW-10) deposed that on 18.10.2018 he was posted as Sub-Divisional Officer of Police in Hoshangabad and investigated Case No. 62/2018, registered in connection with the death of the deceased Aarti.
Based on his investigation, he registered the original crime as Ex.P-17.
During the marg inquiry, he visited the place of occurrence on and prepared the spot map at the instance of Pawan Solanki, which is Ex.P-8.

He seized pieces of Aarti's burnt saree, a half- burnt mangalsutra, a crushed plastic box labeled "Madhur" with the smell of kerosene and other items as detailed in Panchnamas Ex.P-5, Ex.P-6, Ex.P-8, and Ex.P-9, all signed by him.

The sealed house of Aarti was opened and inspected in the presence of witnesses Mukesh and Santosh Bathri and the seizure of additional articles, including burnt matchsticks, a mop, and clothing was documented.
On 10.11.2018 and 24.12.2018, he arrested Maya Solanki and Sanjay alias Sonu Solanki and prepared respective Panchnamas Ex.P-19 and Ex.P-10.

Documents, wedding cards, photographs, registers,
and bills relating to the marriage of Aarti and Pawan (Ex.P-1, Ex.P-20 to Ex.P-30, Articles A-1 to A-10) were seized and recorded.

Statements of witnesses including Mukesh Bathri, Naresh Kumar Bathri, Prembai Bathri, Vrindavan Bathri, Chhotu Malviya, Pawan Solanki, Sanju alias Sonu Solanki and Mayabai Solanki were recorded as per their words.
He sent the seized articles to FSL, Sagar on instructions of Superintendent of Police.
The letter is Ex.P-31 and deposit receipt is Ex.P-32.
This witness admitted in his cross- examination that he received copy of dying declaration of deceased NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:25709 10 CRA-9013-2022 during the inquiry of marg.

He also admitted that during the treatment, the dying declaration had been completed and deceased Aarti stated that when she was working in kitchen and guest had come, she lighten the stove and a matchstick had burnt her saari.

Deceased Aarti also stated in her dying declaration that except for her brother-in-law, her father-in- law, husband, aunt-in-law and grandson were at home, her husband had saved Aarti and she had given her statement without any pressure.
15. Mahima Mishra (DW-1) deposed that he was posted as Naib Tehsildar, Hoshangabad on 29.09.2018.
On that date, she received a complaint from the Hoshangabad Kotwali and she went to the Narmada Hospital Burn Ward ICU, Hoshangabad, where she recorded the dying declaration of injured Aarti Solanki.

entities.text: Narmada Hospital Burn Ward ICU, Hoshangabad
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Prior to recording the statement, she obtained certification from the attending doctor confirming Aarti's ability to give her statement.

She recorded her dying declaration in her own handwriting, in which she stated that while she was lighting the stove in the kitchen as guests had arrived, her saree caught fire, she further stated that her husband had saved her and that she was not under any pressure from anyone while giving her statement.
After recording the said statement, she obtained the thumb impression of injured and also obtained a post-statement certification from the doctor.

The statement is Ex.D-10.
1 6 .
Upon overall consideration of the testimony, several contradictions and omissions emerge between the statements made before the Court and those recorded during investigation.
Vrindavan NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:25709 11 CRA-9013-2022 Bathri (PW-6) admitted that no complaint regarding dowry demand or harassment was made prior to the incident.
He further admitted that the deceased was unable to speak when he met her in the hospital and that no allegation was made immediately after her death.

5 17.

entities.text: State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Sanjay @ Sonu Solanki
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the contrary, the most crucial piece of evidence on record is the dying declaration of the deceased, recorded by an Executive Magistrate (Naib Tehsildar), after obtaining medical certification regarding her fitness.
In the said dying declaration, the deceased has categorically stated that the incident occurred accidentally while she was lighting the stove and that her husband attempted to save her.
She further stated that she was giving the statement voluntarily and without any pressure.
18. In the present case, the allegations of dowry harassment are based on the testimonies of interested witnesses, which suffer from material contradictions and omissions.

No prior complaint regarding cruelty or dowry demand was lodged, and there is no reliable evidence to establish harassment "soon before death," as required under Section 304-B IPC.
1 9 .
In view of the above, serious doubt arises regarding the prosecution story.
The evidence on record does not conclusively establish that the death of the deceased was a dowry death or that it was preceded by cruelty or harassment "soon before death."
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:25709 12 CRA-9013-2022 20.
The learned trial Court, after appreciating the evidence in its proper perspective, has extended the benefit of doubt to the accused persons.
This Court does not find the said view to be perverse or unreasonable.
Rather, it appears to be a plausible view based on the material available on record.
21. All the facts and evidence have been duly appreciated by the learned Trial Court, which has consequently recorded a finding of acquittal.

Such a finding does not warrant any interference,
particularly in light of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Mahabir and Others v. State of Haryana, 2025 SCC OnLine SC 184 , wherein, in paragraph 42, the Apex Court has observed as under:-
"42.

entities.text: Mahabir and Others v. State of Haryana, 2025 SCC OnLine SC 184
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This Court in Ganesha v. Sharanappa, reported in (2014) 1 SCC 87, in para 11,
clarifies that :-
"... Interference with the order of acquittal is called for only in exceptional cases - where there is manifest error of law of procedure resulting into miscarriage of justice,
and, where the acquittal has been caused by shutting out evidence which otherwise ought to have been considered or where material evidence which clinches the issue has been overlooked.

entities.text: Ganesha v. Sharanappa, reported in (2014) 1 SCC 87
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In such exceptional cases, the High Court can set aside an order of acquittal, but it cannot covert it into one of conviction.
The only NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:25709 13 CRA-9013-2022 course left to the High Court in such exception cases, is to order retrial"."

22. In view of aforesaid discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt, and no interference is called for in the impugned judgment of acquittal.
